title: Government at Local Level — Institutions of Local Self-Government
shortDescription: Panchayati Raj (73rd Amendment) and Urban Local Bodies (74th Amendment), committees and Gujarat context.
genZNote: The third tier of government — closest to your gali, your tap and your ration shop. Two amendments, two schedules, a lot of easy marks.

sections.heading: Evolution
bullets: Balwantrai Mehta Committee (1957): three-tier Panchayati Raj; Rajasthan (Nagaur, 2 Oct 1959) first state to adopt it.
Ashok Mehta Committee (1977): two-tier system; L. M. Singhvi and Thungon committees recommended constitutional status.
73rd Amendment (Part IX, Arts. 243–243O) in force 24 April 1993 — now observed as National Panchayati Raj Day; 74th Amendment (Part IX-A, Arts. 243P–243ZG) in force 1 June 1993.

sections.heading: Key Provisions
sections.body: Gram Sabha (Art. 243A) is the body of all registered voters in a village. If a local body is dissolved, fresh elections must be held within 6 months. PESA (1996) extends Panchayat provisions to Fifth Schedule areas. Local government is a State subject (List II).

rows: Gram, intermediate, district (small states may skip intermediate)
Nagar Panchayat, Municipal Council, Municipal Corporation
Direct, every 5 years; State Election Commission (243K / 243ZA)
SC/ST proportional; at least 1/3 women (states may exceed)
District Planning Committee and Metropolitan Planning Committee

sections.heading: Gujarat Context
bullets: Gujarat has a three-tier Panchayati Raj governed by the Gujarat Panchayats Act, 1993 (gram, taluka and district panchayats); urban bodies by the Gujarat Municipalities Act, 1963 and the Gujarat Provincial Municipal Corporations Act, 1949.
Gujarat has increased women's reservation in local bodies beyond one-third (to 50%) — verify the latest provision.
Local bodies elections are conducted by the State Election Commission, Gujarat.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Local self-government institutions were given constitutional status by the 73rd and 74th Amendments, creating rural and urban local bodies with regular elections and finance commissions.
